summary: Full-extraction pass over three IMF Article IV reports (2023, 2025, 2026) and three budget speeches (2023, 2024, 2026) for Antigua and Barbuda. Added the remaining years of the IMF 'o/w CIP revenue' lines (EC$ and % of GDP, including projections), the 2024 budget's Appendix 2 lines for CIP Collections and CIU surplus funds, and two 'nearly 60% of non-tax revenue' shares (new indicator proposed).

observations.quote: receipts from the Citizenship by Investment programme accounted for nearly 60 per cent of non-tax revenue and amounted to $88.8 million
observations.notes: Printed as 'nearly 60 per cent' (rounded, an upper bound). Denominator is non-tax revenue, given in the same paragraph as $154.1 million for 2022; the speech presents 2022 figures as preliminary. Same sentence as the EC$88.8m row.

observations.quote: The Citizenship by Investment programme contributes nearly 60% of non-tax revenue and, even though this contribution is expected to amount to $67 million in 2023
observations.notes: Printed as 'nearly 60%' (rounded, an upper bound), in the present tense; the year is not stated for the share. Recorded as 2023 because the sentence sits in the review of 2023 (non-tax receipts projected at $121.2 million in 2023, and the $67 million expected for 2023 in the same sentence), with period_basis 'unspecified' following the dataset convention.

Line 'of which: CIP Collections' under Non-Tax Revenue in the budget summary (Appendix 2, Central Government Fiscal Operations). Excludes the separate line 'Surplus Funds CIU' (recorded as cbi_transfers_to_government). Breakdown category=cip_collections keeps this line apart from the speech's totals (e.g. $130 million 2024 CIP receipts = 100m collections + 30m CIU surplus). The 2023 budget speech gave EC$88.8m for 2022; IMF tables give 68.

new_indicators.name: CBI share of non-tax revenue
new_indicators.definition: CBI money counted as government revenue in a period divided by the government's non-tax revenue in that period, as stated by the source. Never calculated by us.
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by extract-cbi-atg2 for Antigua and Barbuda budget speeches ('nearly 60 per cent of non-tax revenue'). Kept apart from cbi_fiscal_revenue_pct_revenue because non-tax revenue is a much smaller denominator than total revenue.

ledger.contains: IMF Country Report 24/22 (Jan 2024): press release, staff report text, Tables 1-6 (selected indicators, gross financing needs, central government operations in EC$ and % of GDP, monetary survey, debt, balance of payments), annexes (past advice, risk matrix, external sector, debt sustainability with charts, tourism, global financial conditions) and informational annex. Programme content: 'o/w CIP revenue' line 2018-2028 in Tables 3a (EC$m) and 3b (% of GDP), now all extracted (2018-2022 were already in the data); qualitative remarks on CIP/AML frameworks, CIP agents, outreach to diversify applicants, risk of lower CIP revenue. Out of scope: macro, fiscal, debt and BoP figures; BoP 'Capital transfers' (Table 6) is said in Annex III to be mainly CBI inflows but is not a CBI line, so not extracted. No chart shows CIP.

IMF Country Report 25/96 (Apr 2025): press release, staff report, Tables 1-8, annexes (past advice, external sector, DSA, risk matrix, ECCU revenue/spending comparison, firm productivity, data adequacy). Programme content: 'o/w CIP revenue' line 2020-2029 in Tables 4a (EC$m) and 4b (% of GDP), now all extracted; text: 2025 CIP inflows 'slightly over 1 percent of GDP' (same as Table 4b 2025 cell, not recorded twice); CBI share of total revenue 2023 (9.4%, already in data); higher investment thresholds and CIP Unit/FIU cooperation; signing of the regional CBI agreement (undated; the regional MoA is already in events). Out of scope: macro, fiscal, BoP, other ECCU tax figures; BoP capital transfers (not a CBI line).
ledger.to_do: Charts 'Revenue and Spending for ECCU-6 (2023)' (PDF p. 15) and 'Total Revenue (2023)' in Annex V (PDF p. 56) plot CBI revenue in % of GDP for ATG, DMA, GRD, KNA, LCA and VCT with no printed values; only readable from the chart image (not done, values would be estimates).

ledger.contains: IMF Country Report 26/97 (May 2026): press release, staff report, Tables 1-8, annexes (past advice, external sector, DSA, risk matrix, selected issues on trade/tourism, data), Executive Director's statement. Programme content: 'o/w CIP revenue' line 2021-2031 in Tables 4a (EC$m) and 4b (% of GDP), now all extracted; text on stronger CIP inflows in 2025, CIP capital transfers financing the current account (no figure), data gap on CIP-related FDI, regional CIP regulator enacted ('late 2025' in Annex I, PDF pp. 51-52). Out of scope: macro, fiscal, BoP (capital transfers line not labelled CBI).

Budget speech, 2 March 2023: 2022 economic and fiscal review, 2023 strategy, projects, 2023 revenue and expenditure estimates. Programme content: 2022 CIP receipts EC$88.8m (already in data) and 'nearly 60 per cent of non-tax revenue' (added). No appendices in this copy. Everything else (taxes, spending, debt, projects) is out of scope.

Budget speech, 15 December 2023, with Appendix 1 (budgetary allocations 2024) and Appendix 2 (central government fiscal operations: 2022 actuals, 2023 approved, 2023 preliminary, 2024 budget). Programme content: CIP 'nearly 60% of non-tax revenue' and EC$67m expected 2023 (p. 12); CIP receipts EC$130m budgeted 2024 (p. 34); Appendix 2 lines 'CIP Collections' (4 columns) and 'Surplus Funds CIU' (2 columns), all now extracted. A bar chart on p. 11 ('Performance of Selected Revenue', CIP Receipts actual 2022 / prelim 2023) has no printed values; the same two figures are printed in Appendix 2. Out of scope: other revenue, spending, debt, projects.

Budget speech, 4 December 2025: 2025 review, 2026 priorities and estimates. Programme content: 2025 non-tax revenue includes EC$157m from the CIP (already in data); CIU surplus funds mentioned within EC$48m 'dividends and surpluses' with no separate amount; 2026 non-tax revenue includes '$120 million in CIP receipts and surpluses from state-owned enterprises' (already in data, ambiguity noted on that row). The speech refers to appendices with full estimates, but they are not in this stored copy (ends at p. 51). Everything else is out of scope.
